### Checklist

- [ ] 1. If the issue you raised is not a feature but a question, please raise a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions/new/choose Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] 2. Please use English, otherwise it will be closed.

### Motivation

Hi everyone,

I'm designing and implementing multilingual support for docs.sglang.ai, and have created a preliminary demo that shows potential for supporting numerous languages. This initiative could help native speakers of various languages learn more effectively and adopt SGLang faster. However, this is an early concept requiring significant refinement.

Key challenges to address:

Establishing sustainable contribution workflows
Organizing translation maintenance
Encouraging broader community participation
I welcome all suggestions, particularly from core maintainers, on shaping this project's direction and operational framework.

comments.body:
Hi @samzong 
that is a nice idea and i like it.
A few things we should keep in mind when we somehow want to autogenerate this IMO:

- We should chunk the docs sufficently to ensure good quality of generation, this should not be a big problem for the markdowns as they are structured naturally by sections. We should keep in mind to exclude code sections from translation (or if so, only the comments inside the codeblocks)
- There is a relatively large portions of jupyter notebooks in our docs, for these we would need a more advanced parsing logic. Only the markdown sections should be translated
- Ideally it would be good if we have a verification process if a translation is accurate, i imagine a simple way would be to generate translation -> back translate with separate LLM call -> let separate LLM call determine if translation is accurate.
- It would be good if a human who speaks the languages ensures that the translations are accecaptable additionaly
- How often would we like to trigger automatical translation? I imagine it should be that we only generate new translation if relevant text in docs changes

These are my initial thoughts, what do you thing @samzong @zhaochenyang20 @shuaills
@simveit we can provide grok API to translate. But I think we can translate it per day.
Would it worthwhile to have some sort of maintainer, etc. for each language? auto-translations can be flaky and it would be nice to have reviews at some intervals.

Thanks for all your comments

I'm excited about the docs initiative [https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/tree/main/docs#sglang-documentation](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/tree/main/docs#sglang-documentation) as it lets non-coders like me contribute through documentation. While I can't help with core code, I can be a power user and doc contributor.

First, build a multilingual framework using 1-2 pilot languages (e.g. Chinese/Japanese with English) to standardize localization processes. Projects like Kubernetes show localized docs are key for global adoption.

After native-speaking volunteers finish initial translations, use LLMs (e.g. Grok) for auto-syncing PR translations or periodic updates. Keep human experts for mandatory reviews to ensure accuracy and efficiency.

Manual reviews maintain code blocks (like Jupyter notebooks) integrity and etc.

@zhaochenyang20 @simveit @windsonsea @shuaills @vincent-4 

(I can make a more detail proposal document at later.)
This issue has been automatically closed due to inactivity. Please feel free to reopen it if needed.
